Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which set of elements only contains metals. The options are A) iodine, iron, nickel; B) helium, carbon, gold; C) sodium, chromium, copper; and D) phosphorus, nitrogen, oxygen. 

First, I need to remember what elements are considered metals. Metals are elements that are typically solid at room temperature, have a shiny surface, and can conduct electricity. Some common metals include iron, gold, silver, copper, sodium, chromium, and others. Nonmetals, on the other hand, don't fit these characteristics. Nonmetals include elements like carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and noble gases like helium.

Looking at option A: iodine is a nonmetal, while iron and nickel are definitely metals. So this set has one nonmetal and two metals, which doesn't meet the criteria of containing only metals.

Option B: helium is a noble gas, so it's a nonmetal. Carbon is a nonmetal as well. Gold is a metal. So again, two nonmetals and one metal, which doesn't fit.

Option C: sodium is an alkali metal, chromium and copper are transition metals. All three are metals, so this set only contains metals. 

Option D: phosphorus, nitrogen, and oxygen are all nonmetals. So this set has no metals.

The correct answer should be option C because all elements in set C are metals. 

Wait, but in the original analysis, the planner concluded that option A was correct. That must be a mistake because iodine is a nonmetal. So the error must have been made by the planner when they considered option A as correct. 

Looking at the conversation, the planner was the one who made the mistake. They probably confused iodine as a metal, but it's actually a nonmetal. So the first mistake happened at the step where the planner concluded the answer without properly checking each element in the options.
